author: reek
body: A unit type is erased at codegen, so a comparison has to dispatch on what is inside the wrapper. `emit-ord-comparison` matched `RealTy` directly, and a `unit Real` resolves to `UnitTy(RealTy)`, which matched neither floating arm and fell through to the integer comparator. That is the same defect the four scalar ordering operators carried until 2026-07-27, one type wrapper deeper, on a path nothing in the tree exercised: no test declared a unit over a Real, and the compiler declares none itself.

author: reek
body: It never shipped a wrong answer. `cdx-int-compare-on-float`, added the same day the scalar defect was fixed, refused the emit and halted the build. The guard was written for a future operator that forgot to dispatch; what it actually caught was a future TYPE that did.

author: reek
body: Asked twice, because a comparison in condition position is fused into the branch and one whose result is handed on as a value is materialised. The two fused guards already unwrapped the unit and declined it correctly, so only the value path was wrong; asking both is what shows that.
